description: Restart-recovery scenarios scripts/performance/verify-stage19-resilience.mjs and scripts/performance/lib/recovery-matrix.mjs measure against. Each scenario restarts exactly one Docker Compose service (`docker compose restart <service>`, never --force-recreate, matching how an operator would actually restart a single component) and measures the listed timings plus a state-drift read-back.

scenarios.notes: Static nginx container; no server-side state to drift.
Runtime-control document and kill-switch gate live on a bind-mounted directory, not in the container — must survive a plain restart unchanged.
Demo host frontend's business-API dependency; isolated from the telemetry path by design (Section 13).

Independent container lifecycle sharing openobserve's network namespace (hard SSRF-guard constraint, see compose.yaml); depends_on.restart:true covers the openobserve-restarts-first ordering automatically.
Heaviest, most stateful container. depends_on.restart:true on alert-sink means this scenario also exercises the alert-sink auto-restart path.

Not a container restart — reverse-proxy's runtime-control read path is exercised directly (see docs/runtime-control-and-kill-switch.md) while proxy restarts, to check the operator/kill-switch plane degrades and recovers independently of the browser-facing ingest plane.
A short, reversible `docker network disconnect`/`connect` cycle on one internal service (not iptables, not host-level) simulating a partition, per Section 15's network-failure-injection list.

restartCountExpectation: Every scenario's own docker-compose restart count for its target service must equal exactly 1 (the deliberate restart); no other service's restart count may change as a side effect, except alert-sink's after an openobserve-target scenario (expected, from depends_on.restart:true).
driftPolicy: Any readBack key differing before vs. after a scenario is a Stage 19 finding (Section 20), not a soft warning.
